transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-06-18
Start time: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Alex Martinez (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (HelioBio CTO), Samira Khan (HelioBio SecOps), Evan Park (HelioBio ML)
Links mentioned: https://redwood.example.com/soc2 (SOC2 summary), https://drive.redwood.example.com/helio/audit-sample (audit log sample)

Summary:
Quick sync to review pilot results (latency/cost numbers), confirm compliance gating items (SSO/SAML, audit logging format and retention), and agree next steps for canary run with production traffic. Customer has firm retention & legal hold needs for specific datasets; wants SOC2 evidence and an exportable audit log format.

Topics covered:
- Pilot results recap (latency & token cost)
- SSO / SAML integration status and mapping to RBAC
- Audit logs: fields, export frequency, schema, retention, and secure storage (KMS)
- SOC2 and compliance artifacts (what Redwood can share)
- Data retention, legal hold, and encryption at rest/in transit
- Next steps and scheduling a canary run

Transcript body:
[00:00:00] Alex Martinez: All right, folks, thanks for joining. Uh, we wanted to keep this tight — 45 minutes ish — check on the POC status and, uh, surface any compliance blockers. Jordan, Samira, Evan, you good for agenda?

[00:00:12] Jordan Lee: Yep, sounds good. We just finished baseline runs yesterday, so we'll walk through a couple of items.

[00:00:18] Samira Khan: Yep, I mainly want to make sure audit logs and retention are nailed down. Also SSO, we hit a couple of mapping issues last time.

[00:00:26] Priya Nair: Cool, I'll jump into the audit log schema and where we put the events. Alex will cover the SOC2 / doc stuff and the high level results.

[00:00:37] Alex Martinez: Great. Quick results first — Evan, do you want to share the baseline numbers? We saw median p50 token latency around 120 ms for single-shot generates, throughput pretty stable with our Dedicated dev pool. Cost was within the sweet spot we discussed, about 0.6 cents per gpt-token equivalent — caveat, this is with continuous batching and prefix cache enabled.

[00:01:02] Evan Park: Yeah, that's right. The latency distribution shows a small tail at long sequences, that's where priya's tuning suggestions came in, we reduced kv-cache misses by pinning the model variant and increasing the KV cache size — that helped.

[00:01:18] Jordan Lee: Good. But for us right now the blocker is not performance it's compliance — SSO and retention.

[00:01:26] Samira Khan: Exactly. So two things: one, SAML mapping — we need groups to map to roles in Redwood so our internal RBAC maps to their dataset access. Two, audit logs — we need a daily export that we can ship to our SIEM and also a way to request ad-hoc exports for legal holds.

[00:01:43] Priya Nair: Understood. For SAML we support SP-initiated SSO and metadata exchange. We can map IdP groups to Redwood roles and there is a role mapping file in the console. Note that currently the UI shows roles as text — we can also programmatically push via API for automation.

[00:02:02] Samira Khan: When you say role mapping file, is that a downloadable JSON? We would like to keep it in our managed config repo.

[00:02:09] Priya Nair: Yes, we provide a JSON mapping sample. We'll put it in the shared folder after this call. It contains principal_id, group name, and the target Redwood role string. Worth noting sometimes the IdP uses different attribute names — so you'll want your IdP team to confirm attribute mapping (e.g., urn:oid:...).

[00:02:27] Alex Martinez: I'll add: we also have SSO session timeouts and idle timeouts configurable per org — and we can enforce SCIM provisioning if you want automated deprovisioning.

[00:02:39] Jordan Lee: SCIM would be nice. Our HR system is the source of truth.

[00:02:43] Samira Khan: Can SCIM sync group membership too, or just users?

[00:02:47] Priya Nair: SCIM supports groups in our implementation; it's optional but available. We'll send our SCIM schema.

[00:02:56] Evan Park: On the audit logs, we pushed a sample yesterday to the drive — it's a newline delimited JSON with event_type, timestamp, user_id, session_id, model_id, prompt_hash (anonymized), and outcome.

[00:03:12] Samira Khan: We saw that sample, thanks. Couple items: we need a legal-hold flag field so we can mark rows retained beyond normal retention and we need tamper-evidence/auditable integrity checks — like a signing or checksum mechanism.

[00:03:26] Priya Nair: We can add a legal_hold boolean in the export. For tamper-evidence, we offer signed manifests for exports using HMAC with a customer-managed key if you choose KMS integration on Private. For hosted, we can provide signed export bundles using our service key.

[00:03:44] Samira Khan: Hmm — KMS integration is a must-have for us. Our policy requires customer-managed keys for any sensitive exports. Is that only for Private deployments?

[00:03:50] Alex Martinez: Good question. KMS/HSM customer-managed keys are available in Redwood Private and as an enterprise add-on for Dedicated — for hosted we have envelope encryption but the root key is Redwood-managed. We can scope a dedicated offering during contract negotiations, but for the POC we can provide signed exports from our side so you can validate integrity.

[00:04:08] Jordan Lee: Would signed exports be acceptable as short-term? Our legal team will want to see the SOC2 and a design that shows KMS is planned.

[00:04:16] Alex Martinez: Absolutely, we'll send SOC2 Type II attestation and an architecture note showing KMS plan for Dedicated/Private.

[00:04:23] Samira Khan: Another retention detail: for certain regulated datasets we need a minimum of seven years retention and ability to subset by user or dataset for discovery requests. How does Redwood's retention configuration work?

[00:04:35] Priya Nair: Retention is configurable per-tenant and per-route. You can set sliding windows (30/90/365 days) and exempt items with legal_hold flags. For long-term retention we can offload exports to your S3 bucket encrypted with your KMS key. That way the long-term copy is under your control.

[00:04:51] Evan Park: Practically, we configured a 90-day primary retention for the pilot but have a nightly export job to S3 in the test account. We can change export cadence.

[00:04:59] Samira Khan: Nightly is fine as long as it's atomic and we get manifests. Also need the ability to query logs by user_id and prompt_hash quickly for e-discovery. Any indexing support?

[00:05:10] Priya Nair: Exports are NDJSON but we also have a managed ELK/Datadog connector for real-time ingestion. For querying exported files, we recommend Athena or equivalent — the manifest includes column types. For the POC, we can spin up a demo Athena table for you.

[00:05:27] Jordan Lee: That would help. Evan, can you run a demo query once they spin it up?

[00:05:31] Evan Park: Yep.

[00:05:33] Alex Martinez: Okay shifting a bit — SOC2 artifacts. We'll send the attestation pdf and a short bullet doc describing controls around access, encryption, incident response, patching cadence. It won't be the full audit package but should satisfy initial legal questions.

[00:05:48] Samira Khan: Please include control descriptions for access provisioning/deprovisioning and for log retention. Also ask: does Redwood keep separate immutable audit trails for admin actions?

[00:05:58] Priya Nair: We do keep an immutable admin audit trail for configuration changes. Those records are retained per org and can be exported. They include actor, timestamp, change payload (diff), and request origin IP.

[00:06:12] Samira Khan: Good. Is IP redaction available for privacy-sensitive requests?

[00:06:16] Priya Nair: We can redact or hash IPs in exports on request; defaults keep IPs masked. We'll document the options.

[00:06:25] Jordan Lee: On the SSO side, we ran into an issue mapping our internal "research" group to the Redwood "model-editor" role. The mapping looked like it wasn't syncing group membership during SCIM provisioning.

[00:06:37] Priya Nair: We saw an intermittent SCIM group sync bug in the last minor release but patched it. For your org, we recommended re-provisioning the groups after the fix. I'll attach the release notes and the SCIM schema with the group membership sample.

[00:06:51] Evan Park: We did a manual workaround but automation is desired.

[00:06:55] Alex Martinez: We'll prioritize confirming SCIM stability for your tenant and provide a short runbook for fixes if edge cases appear.

[00:07:04] Samira Khan: For the legal-hold workflow, what is the process to request an ad-hoc export? Is it API driven? Email ticket? We need auditability.

[00:07:12] Priya Nair: There is an admin API to create an export job with parameters (time range, filters, include_legal_hold boolean). It returns a job id and a signed manifest once complete. We can demo the API. For hosted customers without API access, there is a support-assisted export. In your Dedicated test the API is available.

[00:07:29] Jordan Lee: Great. We'll want to test the ad-hoc export and validate the manifest signature.

[00:07:33] Alex Martinez: Priya will provision a sample export with HMAC manifest for you to validate against the sample keys. If you want KMS-based signing, that will require the Dedicated/Private key workflow.

[00:07:45] Samira Khan: On encryption in transit, are there any TLS ciphers we should be aware of? We have a requirement to disallow certain legacy ciphers.

[00:07:53] Priya Nair: We support TLS 1.2+ with modern ciphers; I'll include the cipher suite list in the security pack.

[00:07:59] Jordan Lee: Ok. One more thing — we want rate-limiting and throttling controls per route so research folks can't burn the budget. How granular are those?

[00:08:08] Priya Nair: You can set per-route qps and token caps, plus per-user quotas. We also expose tokens per-call metrics in the console so you can tune. For budget protection we can add a hard cap at the org level.

[00:08:20] Evan Park: For the canary, we'll run a mixed workload of interactive chat + batch scoring. We'll want to exercise rate-limits and retention.

[00:08:29] Alex Martinez: Perfect. Let's map immediate deliverables: I'll send SOC2 artifact and the short controls doc; Priya will drop SCIM/SSO/SCIM schemas and audit sample exports in shared drive; Evan will coordinate the canary schedule with you.

[00:08:43] Samira Khan: Sounds good. Any blockers from Redwood side that would prevent the canary next week?

[00:08:49] Priya Nair: Nothing blocking — we need your SAML metadata and confirm the IdP test endpoint. Also need the list of test users for SCIM.

[00:08:59] Jordan Lee: We'll get that to you by Thursday.

[00:09:02] Alex Martinez: Great. Let's talk risks quickly — the main commercial risk you raised was KMS for hosted. We covered that: short-term signed exports + SOC2, long-term plan for Dedicated/Private with customer-managed KMS. Technical risk: SCIM group sync — patched; we'll validate. Performance risk: tail latency on long sequences — Priya's tuning seems to be working but we'll validate under canary load.

[00:09:26] Samira Khan: All right. Two quick clarifications before we wrap: 1) can we get an example manifest signature verification script? 2) will the audit export include prompt text or just hashes?

[00:09:38] Priya Nair: We'll provide a small verification script (python) that validates the HMAC signature using a shared secret. Regarding prompt text, by default exports include prompt_hash only; full prompt text can be included if you enable retention for that route and agree to data residency and access controls. We redact PII by default in sample exports.

[00:09:57] Samira Khan: Understood. For the pilot we want prompt_hash only, but for e-discovery we may need the full prompt text for the legal team — in that case we'll coordinate a controlled export.

[00:10:06] Alex Martinez: Noted. We'll document the workflows and controls for that.

[00:10:11] Jordan Lee: Ok let's recap next steps — Alex SOC2 + controls doc; Priya audit sample + SCIM + manifest verifier; Evan schedule canary and run queries post-export. Helio to send SAML metadata and confirm retention/legal-hold rules.

[00:10:26] Alex Martinez: Perfect. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the documents and set up the canary slot.

[00:10:34] Samira Khan: Thanks, talk soon.

[00:10:37] Meeting ended.

Notes on transcription: occasional names or acronyms may be slightly off (e.g., SCIM vs S-C-I-M spelled out), product labels: Redwood Dedicated printed as "Dedicated dev pool" or sometimes "Redwood Dedicate" in transcript. There are short pauses and crosstalk.
